raw_case_text:
A 29 year old previously asymptomatic male was admitted in a peripheral hospital with fever and jaundice of 1 week duration. He had anemia (hemoglobin [Hb] 8.8 g/dl), thromocytopenia (platelet count 55,000/mul), renal impairment (serum creatinine [s. creatinine] 1.5 mg/dl) and direct hyperbilirubinemia (total bilirubin 3.9 mg/dl, direct 1.9 mg/dl). Peripheral smear showed the presence of schizonts of Plasmodium vivax. Antigen test for Plasmodium falciparum was negative. He was treated with Artesunate and Clindamycin for 7 days and was discharged when asymptomatic, although improvement in thrombocytopenia or renal impairment was not observed. Two week later (1 week after being afebrile and getting discharged) he presented to us with vomiting and pain in the abdomen for 3 days and decreased urine output. He did not have fever, loose motions, rash, bleeding or alteration in sensorium. There was no history of treatment with quinine. He was hypertensive, pale, did not have edema and had unremarkable systemic examination except for the presence of haemic murmur. Severe anemia (hemoglobin 4.8 g/dl), thrombocytopenia (platelet count 61,000/mul) and azotemia (s. creatinine 8.3 mg/dl) were noted. Presence of schistocytes on peripheral smear, elevated reticulocyte count (13%), elevated serum lactate dehydrogenase (LDH 1242 U/L) and indirect hyperbilirubinaemia indicated ongoing microangiopathic hemolytic anemia. Urinalysis showed microhematuria and proteinuria of 3.75 g/day. Coagulation profile was normal. Serum C3 level was low (50 mg/dl), C4 level being normal. Antinuclear antibodies and enzyme-linked immuno sorbent assay for human immunodeficiency virus were negative. Hepatitis B surface antigen and anti-hepatitis C antibodies were negative. He underwent five sessions of 1.5 volume plasma exchanges with replacement with fresh frozen plasma. Hypertension was controlled. Intermittent hemodialysis was done. Anemia was corrected with packed red cells transfusion. After five sessions of plasma exchanges, platelet count increased to 150,000/mul Hb stabilized at 6 g/dl and then increased. S. LDH decreased to 206.3 U/L and s. creatinine stabilized at 5.5 mg/dl, patient being dialysis-independent. This hematological remission persisted at 4th week (Hb 9.1 g/dl, platelet count 163,000/mul) with C3 level being normal. Kidney biopsy was performed at this time. Enlarged glomeruli had capillary wall thickening, with double contours seen on silver Methanamine stain, endothelial swelling and increased mesangial cellularity. Arterioles with onion peel appearance were seen [Figures 1 and 2]. No immune deposit was seen on immunoflorescence study.
At the end of 4 months, he requires two antihypertensive drugs, has Hb 13.5 g/dl, platelet count 229,000/mul, s. creatinine 1.4 mg/dl and poteinuria 1.2 g/day.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 29-year-old male presenting with abdominal pain, vomiting, severe oliguria, and extreme pallor 2 weeks after initial treatment for a febrile icteric illness.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: Two weeks prior to presentation, the patient was treated at a peripheral hospital for 1 week of fever and jaundice, receiving a 7-day course of artesunate and clindamycin. Although his fever resolved and he was discharged, laboratory abnormalities had not fully normalized. One week post-discharge, he developed persistent vomiting, abdominal pain, and progressive oliguria over 3 days without recurrent fevers, diarrhea, or gross bleeding, prompting referral to a nephrology service.
subjective.past_medical_history: Treated with artesunate and clindamycin for 7 days 2 weeks prior for a febrile illness with jaundice, thrombocytopenia, and mild renal impairment. No prior hypertension or renal disease. Denied prior exposure to quinine.
subjective.review_of_systems: Positive for nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain, oliguria, and profound fatigue. Negative for fever, diarrhea, hematuria, hemoptysis, rash, or altered sensorium. Medications: artesunate and clindamycin completed 1 week prior. Allergies: null.

objective.physical_examination: Blood pressure: elevated (hypertensive), afebrile. Marked pallor without peripheral edema or icterus. Cardiovascular: Hemic flow murmur; normal heart sounds. Abdominal, respiratory, and neurological examinations were otherwise unremarkable.
objective.routine_investigations: Initial peripheral hospital labs: Hemoglobin: 8.8 g/dL, platelet count: 55,000/muL, serum creatinine: 1.5 mg/dL, total bilirubin: 3.9 mg/dL (direct bilirubin: 1.9 mg/dL). Readmission labs: Hemoglobin: 4.8 g/dL, platelet count: 61,000/muL, serum creatinine: 8.3 mg/dL. Peripheral blood smear: Presence of schistocytes, reticulocyte count: 13%. Serum lactate dehydrogenase (LDH): 1,242 U/L (declined to 206.3 U/L post-plasmapheresis). Urinalysis: Microscopic hematuria, proteinuria: 3.75 g/24 hours. Coagulation profile: Normal. Complement levels: Serum C3 low at 50 mg/dL, C4 normal (C3 normalized at 4 weeks). Autoimmune and viral serologies: Antinuclear antibodies (ANA), HIV ELISA, HBsAg, and anti-HCV antibodies all negative. Hematologic recovery at 4 weeks: Hemoglobin 9.1 g/dL, platelet count 163,000/muL; at 4 months: Hemoglobin 13.5 g/dL, platelet count 229,000/muL, serum creatinine 1.4 mg/dL, proteinuria 1.2 g/day.
objective.advanced_workup: Percutaneous renal biopsy: Enlarged glomeruli with capillary wall thickening, double contours on silver methenamine stain, endothelial swelling, and increased mesangial cellularity; arterioles demonstrated prominent 'onion-peel' intimal hyperplasia; immunofluorescence negative for immune complex deposits, confirming thrombotic microangiopathy (TMA).

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation:
Definitive diagnosis: Acute Plasmodium vivax infection triggering secondary atypical hemolytic uremic syndrome / thrombotic microangiopathy (TMA/HUS) with severe acute kidney injury.
Diagnostic confirmation: Initial peripheral smear demonstrated schizonts of Plasmodium vivax; rapid antigen test for Plasmodium falciparum was negative. Microangiopathic hemolytic anemia and renal TMA were confirmed by peripheral schistocytes, elevated LDH, reticulocytosis, severe azotemia, low C3, and classic histologic features on renal biopsy.
Plan & Outcome: Completed initial antiparasitic therapy with artesunate and clindamycin. TMA and acute renal failure managed with five sessions of 1.5-volume therapeutic plasma exchange (TPE) with fresh frozen plasma replacement, packed red blood cell transfusions, temporary intermittent hemodialysis, and antihypertensive therapy. Hematologic remission and dialysis independence were achieved, with creatinine stabilizing to 1.4 mg/dL at 4 months on two antihypertensive agents.
